title: Character & Conduct
description: General User → Mid. Familiar character teachings, broader basics and short everyday applications. Covers fair testimony, reconciliation, responsible speech, confidences, gratitude, kindness, financial responsibilities and dignity. All questions are Mid level; specialist disputes and individual legal rulings are outside the scope.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires more understanding and simple connections than Beginner, without specialist study. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: According to Quran 4:135, whose interests must not stop a believer from giving truthful testimony?

options.text: Their own or their close relatives' interests
Only the interests of strangers
Only the interests of wealthy people
Only the interests of people they dislike

questions.explanation: The verse calls for justice even when truthful testimony is against oneself, parents or close relatives.

questions.question: What does Quran 49:10 encourage when believers are in conflict?

options.text: Treating every disagreement as permanent
Making peace between them
Waiting for the more popular person to win
Taking sides before hearing what happened

questions.explanation: The verse connects the brotherhood of believers with making peace between them.

questions.question: Which behavior does the Quran warn can spoil a person's charity?

options.text: Giving without announcing the amount
Helping someone who cannot repay the favor
Reminding recipients of favors and hurting them
Giving without asking for public praise

questions.explanation: The verse warns against undermining charity through reminders of generosity and hurtful treatment.

questions.question: Which behavior is listed among the signs of hypocrisy in the cited hadith?

options.text: Needing help with a task
Forgetting a person's name
Having little money to give
Betraying a trust

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against lying, breaking promises and betraying trusts. It calls for correcting these traits, not casually judging another person's inner faith.

questions.question: What is namimah, the harmful conduct warned against in the cited chapter?

options.text: Carrying people's words between them to stir up trouble
Quietly seeking help to prevent harm
Conveying an agreed invitation
Passing on a useful public announcement

questions.explanation: Namimah is malicious tale-carrying that damages relationships. It is different from a necessary, responsible report of harm.

questions.question: What should a visitor do after asking permission to enter three times without receiving it?

options.text: Assume silence gives permission
Return rather than keep pressing for entry
Keep knocking until someone answers
Enter if the door is unlocked

questions.explanation: The report teaches returning when permission has not been given after three requests.

questions.question: What treatment does Quran 60:8 permit toward people who have not fought Muslims for their faith or expelled them?

options.text: Kindness only if they first convert
Fairness only in front of witnesses
Kindness and fairness
Deliberate humiliation because their beliefs differ

questions.explanation: The verse affirms kind and fair treatment of the people it describes, despite differences in faith.

questions.question: What does Quran 4:86 teach about responding to a greeting?

options.text: Respond only when the greeter has higher status
Ignore it unless the person repeats it
Return a weaker greeting to show superiority
Return it with a better greeting or a similar one

questions.explanation: The verse teaches a gracious response to a greeting, either better or equivalent.

questions.question: What response to evil does Quran 41:34 encourage?

options.text: Responding with what is better
Always matching an insult word for word
Treating every disagreement as a lasting feud
Choosing whichever reply gains the most applause

questions.explanation: The verse encourages answering evil with better conduct, opening a way toward improved relations.

questions.question: Alongside praising pardon and reconciliation, what do these verses recognize?

options.text: An unlimited right to harm others in revenge
The right of a wronged person to seek justice
A requirement to hide every wrongdoing
That seeking any protection is always blameworthy

questions.explanation: The passage praises pardon while recognizing redress after wrongdoing. It does not authorize excessive retaliation.

questions.question: Instead of craving what Allah has given others, what does Quran 4:32 tell believers to do?

options.text: Demand that others lose their blessings
Assume another person's success is an insult
Ask Allah for His bounty
Stop making any effort to improve

questions.explanation: The verse directs attention away from resentful comparison and toward asking Allah for His bounty.

questions.question: What did Anas do with the secret entrusted to him by the Prophet?

options.text: He told it to everyone who asked
He announced it after receiving a gift
He shared it to prove he knew the Prophet
He did not disclose it, even when asked by Umm Sulaym

questions.explanation: Anas's account illustrates care in preserving a confidence entrusted to him.

questions.question: Which action does the cited hadith connect with gratitude to Allah?

options.text: Thanking people for their kindness
Denying that anyone has helped us
Thanking only people who can help again
Avoiding all words of appreciation

questions.explanation: The report teaches that gratitude to Allah goes together with acknowledging kindness from people.

questions.question: How does the cited hadith describe delaying debt repayment by someone able to pay?

options.text: A harmless way to test the lender
An injustice
A form of charity by the borrower
Acceptable whenever the lender is wealthy

questions.explanation: The warning concerns avoidable delay by a debtor who has the means to repay.

questions.question: Which treatment of a worker receives a severe warning in the cited hadith?

options.text: Paying the agreed wage after the work is completed
Clearly explaining the agreed task
Taking the worker's full work but withholding their pay
Acknowledging the worker's contribution

questions.explanation: The report includes an employer who takes the benefit of a worker's labor but does not pay them among those facing Allah's opposition.

questions.question: Which dishonest practice is condemned at the start of Surah al-Mutaffifin?

options.text: Checking a scale before using it
Agreeing clearly on the quantity being sold
Giving the buyer the full amount purchased
Taking full measure when buying but giving less when selling

questions.explanation: The verses condemn the double standard of demanding one's own due while short-changing others.

questions.question: Which act did the Prophet repeatedly warn against among the gravest sins?

options.text: Giving false testimony
Admitting uncertainty about an event
Declining to invent details
Correcting a mistaken statement

questions.explanation: The report emphasizes the seriousness of false testimony through the Prophet's repeated warning.

questions.question: In the hadith describing religion as nasihah, which meaning best fits this term?

options.text: Winning every public argument
Sincerity, including sincere concern for others
Agreeing with everything a friend does
Seeking praise through advice

questions.explanation: Nasihah involves sincerity. In dealings with people, this includes genuine concern for their good, rather than advice used to display superiority.

questions.question: In the story of the thirsty dog, which action was rewarded?

options.text: Ignoring it because it could not repay the favor
Waiting for an audience before helping
Giving the thirsty animal water
Driving it away from available water

questions.explanation: The Prophet described a man forgiven after giving a thirsty dog water and affirmed reward in caring for living creatures.

questions.question: What does the cited hadith say Allah looks at rather than people's appearance and wealth?

options.text: Their social rank alone
Their popularity alone
Their expensive clothing alone
Their hearts and deeds

questions.explanation: The report directs attention to the heart and actions rather than outward appearance or possessions.

questions.question: Why can loyalty to family not justify changing truthful testimony?

options.text: Justice applies even when the truth is personally uncomfortable
Family reputation is always more important than facts
Truth is required only when strangers are involved
A relative's request turns falsehood into truth

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly includes oneself and close relatives in its command to stand firmly for justice.

questions.question: What makes an attempt to reconcile people consistent with these verses?

options.text: Requiring the quieter person to accept every demand
Seeking a fair resolution rather than merely protecting the stronger side
Deciding the more popular side cannot be wrong
Treating a quick agreement as more important than fairness

questions.explanation: The passage calls for making peace with justice. Reconciliation should not become a cover for unfairness.

questions.question: Why is repeatedly saying you owe me after giving charity a serious problem?

options.text: A recipient must repay every charitable gift
Only the size of a gift matters
It turns help into hurtful reminders of the donor's favor
A donor always owns the recipient's future choices

questions.explanation: The verse warns that reminders and hurt can undermine charity. Giving does not justify humiliating the recipient.

questions.question: How should the warning about hypocrisy's traits guide a person's self-assessment?

options.text: Assume good intentions make dishonest habits harmless
Use one observed mistake to claim knowledge of another person's heart
Treat the warning as relevant only to strangers
Examine and correct their own lying, broken promises and betrayal

questions.explanation: The report identifies harmful traits to avoid. Applying it responsibly includes self-correction rather than careless labels about others' inner belief.

questions.question: Why can repeating someone's words still be harmful even when the words are accurate?

options.text: Passing them on to inflame conflict can be malicious tale-carrying
Accurate words can never be misused
Only invented statements can damage relationships
Being asked to repeat something removes all responsibility

questions.explanation: The warning concerns harmful tale-carrying, not only fabrication. Purpose and likely harm matter when deciding what to pass on.

questions.question: What does the instruction to return after three unanswered requests protect?

options.text: The visitor's right to enter whenever curious
The household's ability to decide whether to receive a visitor
A requirement to explain all private circumstances
The belief that knowing someone cancels permission

questions.explanation: The instruction makes clear that a visitor is not entitled to force a response or entry.

questions.question: Does having a different religion by itself prevent the kindness described in Quran 60:8?

options.text: Yes, all kindness must wait until conversion
Yes, only trade without fairness is allowed
No, the verse permits kindness and fairness toward the non-hostile people it describes
Yes, ordinary goodwill is always forbidden

questions.explanation: The verse separates differences in belief from the hostile actions it names and permits kind, fair dealings.

questions.question: Which attitude is most consistent with returning a greeting graciously?

options.text: Saving all courtesy for influential people
Treating a greeting as a demand for a favor
Using the reply to embarrass the greeter
Acknowledging the other person rather than making status the measure of courtesy

questions.explanation: The verse calls for an equivalent or better response; it does not make wealth or popularity the condition for courtesy.

questions.question: Does responding with better conduct mean a person must remain exposed to ongoing harm?

options.text: No, good conduct can go together with seeking protection and justice
Yes, seeking any protection contradicts good character
Yes, every threat must be ignored
No, because every insult requires a harsher insult

questions.explanation: The verses encourage better conduct while allowing a wronged person to speak about wrongdoing. Kindness does not require silence about ongoing harm.

questions.question: Which statement best balances pardon and justice in these verses?

options.text: Pardon makes all forms of protection forbidden
Pardon is praised, and seeking justice must stay within proper limits
Being wronged permits unlimited retaliation
Anyone seeking a fair remedy must have bad character

questions.explanation: The passage praises pardon and reconciliation, recognizes redress and rejects wrongdoing. None of these permits excess.

questions.question: What is a better response to someone else's blessing than resentful comparison?

options.text: Treat their success as evidence of your failure
Insist blessings must be identical for everyone
Ask Allah for good without wishing the blessing taken away
Assume asking Allah for good is pointless

questions.explanation: The verse discourages coveting others' advantages and encourages asking Allah for His bounty.

questions.question: What does Anas's refusal to reveal the Prophet's secret show about curiosity from others?

options.text: Every question creates a duty to disclose
A close relationship always cancels confidentiality
Secrets should be shared whenever the listener insists
Being asked does not by itself cancel an entrusted confidence

questions.explanation: The account illustrates maintaining a confidence despite a request to disclose it. This concerns entrusted information, not concealing danger or abuse.

questions.question: Does thanking Allah mean we should avoid thanking someone who helped us?

options.text: No, gratitude to people fits gratitude to Allah
Yes, appreciating a person's help is always forbidden
Yes, help must be treated as if no person was involved
No, but thanks matter only when money was given

questions.explanation: The hadith connects gratitude to Allah with thanking people. Appreciating their help does not make them independent of Allah.

questions.question: What distinction matters when considering delayed debt repayment?

options.text: Every delay proves the borrower is dishonest
Deliberate delay by someone able to pay differs from genuine hardship
A wealthy borrower never needs to repay
Genuine hardship removes the need for considerate treatment

questions.explanation: The hadith condemns avoidable delay by someone able to pay. The verse calls for time to be given to a debtor in real difficulty.

questions.question: Why is an employer's praise not a substitute for a worker's earned pay?

options.text: Compliments automatically cancel every wage agreement
A worker's effort becomes a free gift after praise
Appreciation does not remove the worker's right to payment
Only workers with high social status deserve payment

questions.explanation: The warning concerns taking a worker's labor without paying them. Kind words cannot replace what is owed.

questions.question: What double standard do these verses expose?

options.text: Using the same accurate measure for everyone
Checking quantities before completing a sale
Correcting an accidental shortage
Demanding one's own full rights while withholding other people's due

questions.explanation: The verses condemn those who insist on full measure for themselves but give others less.

questions.question: Why does wanting to help a friend not justify false testimony?

options.text: A good intention does not turn a false statement into truthful evidence
Friendship makes every supporting statement true
Only testimony against a stranger needs to be accurate
The witness's confidence matters more than what happened

questions.explanation: The hadith condemns false testimony. Personal loyalty does not make a false account acceptable.

questions.question: What best distinguishes sincere advice from advice used to show superiority?

options.text: Making the correction as embarrassing as possible
Seeking the person's good and speaking with appropriate gentleness
Measuring success only by who wins the argument
Giving advice only when praise is guaranteed

questions.explanation: Sincere concern and gentleness support helpful correction. The purpose should be the person's good rather than the adviser gaining attention.

questions.question: What does the thirsty dog's story teach about the scope of mercy?

options.text: Only kindness to people has any moral value
Helping an animal matters only if it belongs to you
Kindness to animals can be a rewarded good deed
A creature must be able to thank us before we help

questions.explanation: The report extends reward for caring to living creatures and illustrates this through helping a thirsty dog.

questions.question: Why is a person's wealth an unreliable measure of spiritual worth?

options.text: Wealth reveals every hidden intention
Expensive clothes guarantee acceptance of all deeds
A good reputation makes actions irrelevant
The hadith directs attention to hearts and deeds

questions.explanation: The report shifts the measure away from appearance and possessions. It includes both the heart and deeds, so actions still matter.

questions.question: Your relative asks you to alter an account of an incident to protect the family. What should you do?

options.text: Give an accurate account rather than change the facts
Change only the facts that make your relative look bad
Let the relative choose what you say happened
Assume family loyalty requires a false account

questions.explanation: The verse requires truthful, just testimony even when it affects close relatives.

questions.question: Two friends have a minor dispute and both want your help. Which approach supports reconciliation?

options.text: Pass each one's angry remarks to the other
Hear both sides and help them reach a fair resolution
Let the more popular friend set every condition
Pressure one to apologize before hearing the facts

questions.explanation: Fair peacemaking seeks to repair a relationship without favoring one side unfairly.

questions.question: After helping someone, you feel tempted to keep reminding them in front of others. What should change?

options.text: Repeat the amount whenever they disagree with you
Demand public praise each time you meet
Stop using the gift as a reason to shame or control them
Treat their private choices as yours to control

questions.explanation: The warning against reminders and hurt applies after a gift as well as at the moment of giving.

questions.question: You notice that you often make promises with no intention of keeping them. What response fits the warning in the hadith?

options.text: Assume a pleasant tone makes the habit harmless
Focus only on finding similar faults in others
Keep promising because spoken commitments never matter
Take the habit seriously and work to become trustworthy

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against promise-breaking as a trait of hypocrisy. Its warning should prompt correction of one's own conduct.

questions.question: A friend asks you to carry insulting remarks to another person just to provoke a quarrel. What should you do?

options.text: Refuse to fuel the quarrel or pass on the insults
Pass them on because repeating is never a choice
Add extra remarks to make the message clearer
Share them publicly so the quarrel grows

questions.explanation: This is a direct example of malicious tale-carrying that damages relationships, rather than a report needed to prevent harm.

questions.question: On an ordinary visit with no emergency, you ask permission three times and receive no answer. What should you do?

options.text: Open the unlocked door and walk in
Leave rather than keep demanding entry
Keep ringing until someone feels forced to answer
Ask a neighbor how to enter through the back

questions.explanation: The report instructs a visitor to return when permission has not been granted after three requests.

questions.question: A peaceful neighbor of another faith needs ordinary practical help. Which response fits Quran 60:8?

options.text: Refuse solely because their faith differs
Offer help only if they first change religion
Offer suitable help with kindness and fairness
Use the situation to humiliate their beliefs

questions.explanation: The verse permits kind and fair dealings with people who have not fought Muslims for their faith or expelled them.

questions.question: A Muslim classmate greets you with salam. Which response follows the verse's guidance?

options.text: Ignore it because the classmate is not popular
Reply only if someone important is watching
Wait until they first do you a favor
Return the salam with an equivalent or fuller greeting

questions.explanation: The verse teaches responding to a greeting with one that is better or similar.

questions.question: Someone makes a minor rude comment during a safe conversation. Which reply best reflects responding with better conduct?

options.text: Answer calmly and avoid returning the insult
Find a more personal insult to use
Recruit others to mock them
Keep repeating the comment to prolong the quarrel

questions.explanation: For this minor, safe situation, a calm response applies the encouragement to answer bad conduct with better conduct.

questions.question: Someone says reporting ongoing bullying always contradicts forgiveness. What is the best response?

options.text: Forgiveness requires accepting every future act of bullying
A person may seek protection and a fair remedy without acting unjustly
Only unlimited revenge is allowed after bullying
A victim must conceal all harm to show good character

questions.explanation: The verses praise pardon while recognizing redress after wrongdoing. Seeking appropriate protection is compatible with avoiding unjust retaliation.

questions.question: A friend's success leaves you wishing they would lose what they gained. What is a better response?

options.text: Feed the resentment until the friendship ends
Treat the friend's happiness as an attack
Ask Allah for good instead of wishing away the friend's blessing
Assume another person's success leaves no good for you

questions.explanation: The verse redirects resentful comparison toward asking Allah for His bounty.

questions.question: A friend entrusts you with harmless private news. Others ask you to reveal it for entertainment. What should you do?

options.text: Reveal it because several people asked
Post it without the friend's name and assume that settles it
Tell one person and ask them to spread it carefully
Keep the confidence unless the friend permits sharing

questions.explanation: Anas's account illustrates preserving a confidence. This scenario concerns harmless private news, not information about danger or abuse.

questions.question: A colleague helps you finish a difficult task. Which response fits the cited teaching?

options.text: Thank them sincerely while recognizing Allah's blessings
Avoid thanking them because you thank Allah
Claim the help made no difference
Thank them only if they agree to help again

questions.explanation: Acknowledging a person's kindness puts the hadith's teaching about gratitude into practice.

questions.question: You can repay a debt that is due but consider delaying only to keep the money longer. What should you do?

options.text: Delay because the lender seems comfortable
Repay what is due rather than delay without justification
Wait until repeated requests become embarrassing
Assume having money makes the debt optional

questions.explanation: The hadith condemns delaying repayment by someone who has the means to pay.

questions.question: An employer accepts the agreed completed work but decides not to pay because the worker has little influence. What is required?

options.text: Treat low status as permission to withhold wages
Replace the wage with a compliment
Honor the worker's right to the agreed payment
Assume completed work becomes free after acceptance

questions.explanation: The cited warning concerns obtaining a worker's labor and then withholding their pay. Social influence does not remove that right.

questions.question: A shopkeeper's scale deliberately gives customers less than the quantity they pay for. What should change?

options.text: Keep the scale if buyers rarely notice
Use accurate weights only for regular customers
Add a friendly greeting instead of correcting the shortage
Use an accurate scale and give the full amount owed

questions.explanation: The verses directly condemn giving buyers less in weighing or measuring.

questions.question: A friend wants you to say you witnessed an event you did not see. What should you do?

options.text: Refuse to claim firsthand knowledge you do not have
Agree if the friend seems certain
Repeat their account as your own memory
Invent only the details needed to support them

questions.explanation: False testimony is gravely warned against. Helping a friend cannot justify pretending to have witnessed something.

questions.question: A friend asks for help correcting a mistake. Which response best expresses sincere advice?

options.text: Use the opportunity to display superiority
Offer accurate, gentle guidance aimed at helping them improve
Praise the mistake to avoid all discomfort
Make their embarrassment the main goal

questions.explanation: Sincerity seeks the person's good, and gentleness helps correction serve that purpose.

questions.question: You can safely provide water for a thirsty animal without causing harm. Which choice reflects the hadith's lesson?

options.text: Wait for someone to promise a reward
Ignore it because it cannot thank you
Provide the water as an act of mercy
Make helping depend on the animal having an owner

questions.explanation: The report affirms reward in caring for living creatures and illustrates it through giving water to a thirsty dog.

questions.question: Someone claims a wealthy, stylish person must be closer to Allah than a poor person. Which response fits the hadith?

options.text: Clothing alone proves the state of the heart
Wealth guarantees that every action is good
People without wealth cannot have spiritual worth
Appearance and wealth do not establish that; hearts and deeds matter

questions.explanation: The hadith makes hearts and deeds central rather than outward appearance and possessions. We cannot rank people's inner worth from wealth alone.
